fatal_errors: The proposed LPBF triple-pass remelting method is unrelated to the demonstrated liquid-metal dealloying treatment in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h.
It omits the directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor and preferential replacement of Ti/V-rich interdendritic channels.

The mechanism incorrectly claims that remelting reduces the effect of positive mixing enthalpy; it does not explain selective Ti–Cu exchange, retention of W/Ta/V ligaments, or formation of the W-rich passivating interlayer.
The claimed 30% reaction-rate increase and 25% stability improvement are fabricated and unsupported by evidence.
The stated temperature and pressure boundaries are arbitrary and do not correspond to the processing or testing conditions.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the broad challenge of combining an RHEA with Cu and proposes a potentially distinct manufacturing idea, but it does not reconstruct the target method, material state, conditions, architecture, mechanism, or outcomes. The target uses liquid-metal dealloying to exploit chemical selectivity in a directionally segregated WTaVTi alloy, producing aligned Cu channels, retained BCC RHEA ligaments, and a W-rich interfacial layer. No evidence supports the LPBF proposal or its numerical performance claims. The proposed comparison is only weakly discriminating because 'reaction rate,' 'microstructural stability,' and the traditional-manufacturing baseline are not operationally defined.
